comment: Channels (cli, api, mcp) of a project and how the user connects them. Nothing here installs, starts or logs in anything; the tools only read it. A key VALUE never appears in this file or in the repository: values live in the OS credential store under the stored name KEYSTORE_<SERVICE>_<ALIAS>; this catalog lists NAMES only. Fields: verified=false means a fact below is not confirmed and the channel is NOT offered by the tools; a nonempty excluded field means the channel is excluded; key.env is the canonical environment variable name the consumer reads (the ONE key name of the service); key.aliases are other names of the same service (duplicates are found by them); key.scope per-device means the key is never copied between machines; key.billingSwitch means the key changes who pays for a client, so it is injected only when named explicitly; key.usedBy lists files that read the key (an empty list means: retire the key if nothing else uses it); install.verified=false means the package name or version is not confirmed here and the command is not offered. Install pins were observed offline with npm ls -g and uv tool list; check the current version before installing. login.check.semantic exit0-logged-in means the command exits 0 only when logged in (shown by the vendor help, behaviour on a logged-out machine NOT verified here). The mcp entries come from docs/ops/mcp-catalog.json: only the MCP entries are mirrored, skills are not channels.

keyNaming.rule: one key per (service, account); a second alias for the same service needs --second-account
